rationale: Applied from dhis2 in merge mode (NDoH DHIS2 (production) 2177 (dhis2)). Lanes were not touched: the source system has no view of the transport network.

A vessel's hold is shared across every facility on its run. Capacity is apportioned by demand share and the trip cost is expressed as a freight rate per cubic metre computed over the whole loop, so no facility is charged for a return journey the boat did not make on its behalf.

Port Moresby has no road connection to Lae, Madang or the Highlands. Primary distribution to every hub other than Port Moresby is modelled as maritime, with the Highlands supplied by road from Lae along the Highlands Highway.

No OSRM instance is configured in this deployment, so road distances are great circle distances inflated by a terrain-specific detour factor: 1.35 mainland, 1.75 highlands, 1.45 coastal. Sea legs use 1.22, river 1.55, air 1.0.

Every sailing and flight frequency, hold capacity and reliability figure is assumed. Confirming whether digitised maritime and air schedules exist for medical distribution is a Sprint 0 task, and the answer determines whether the scheduled-service model has any data behind it.

Facility storage is assumed as days of cover by terrain class: 60 mainland, 45 highlands, 40 coastal, 30 riverine, 26 air-only, 24 island, multiplied by facility type. Replace with the national cold chain inventory and a storage assessment.

Demand is derived from catchment population and a per-1000 consumption rate per product. Replace with mSupply issues data. This is the same proxy-indicator strategy SCANIT uses, and it is a good one — but it must be labelled.
Facility locations, provinces, modes and network structure are real. Demand, storage, costs and every timetable are placeholders with plausible magnitudes.
